key_insight: A physics-informed DeepONet can learn linear-elastic displacement fields directly from geometry and boundary conditions while enforcing fracture traction-free physics without finite-element training data.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast surrogate prediction for real-time structural health monitoring of fractured elastic components, reducing reliance on costly numerical simulations.
method: Encode fracture geometry with a dedicated representation and combine it with boundary-condition inputs.
Train a physics-informed DeepONet to map these inputs to displacement fields.
Impose traction-free fracture conditions weakly using a localized penalty term.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a numerical example on one representative fracture geometry, showing feasibility of the formulation rather than broad benchmark validation.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a single fracture geometry, so generalization across diverse geometries still needs careful validation and robust encoding design.
paper_title: Learning Physics-Informed Surrogate Model of Linear Elastic Displacement Fields from Geometry
